question.text: The diagram above shows the function $y=f(x).$ Which of the following gives the graph of $y=f\left(3(x+2)\right)?$
question.explanation:
To perform transformations of functions with multiple operations, we must remember the following rule:

  1. First, we perform the transformations inside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out horizontal stretches, followed by horizontal translations.

  2. Then, we perform the transformations outside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out vertical stretches, followed by vertical translations.

To plot $y=f\left(3\left(x+2\right)\right),$ we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=f(x).$

  • Stretch it by a scale factor of $\dfrac{1}{\left(3\right)} = \dfrac13$ parallel to the $x$-axis to get the graph of $y=f\left(3x\right).$

  • Then, translate it left by $2$ units to get the graph of $y=f\left(3\left(x+2\right)\right).$

example.title: Graph Transformations Containing Horizontal Translations and Stretches Only

question.text: The diagram above shows the function $y=f(x).$ Which of the following gives the graph of $y=f(x-1)+3?$
question.explanation:
To perform transformations of functions with multiple operations, we must remember the following rule:

  1. First, we perform the transformations inside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out horizontal stretches, followed by horizontal translations.

  2. Then, we perform the transformations outside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out vertical stretches, followed by vertical translations.

To plot $y= f(x-1)+3,$ we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=f(x).$

  • Translate it right by $1$ unit to get the graph of $y=f(x-1).$

  • Then, translate it up by $3$ units to get the graph of $y=f(x-1)+3.$
